title: Decode Ways
description:
A message is a nonempty string of decimal digits. It was formed by joining letter codes: 1 means A, 2 means B, and so on through 26 meaning Z. Return the number of ways to split the entire message into valid codes. Every digit must belong to exactly one code; codes have one or two digits, and a code may not start with zero. The empty string is outside the input domain.

At each prefix, valid decodings end either with its final nonzero digit as a one-digit code or with its final two digits as a code between 10 and 26. Those two choices draw on the preceding prefix counts and are disjoint. A zero cannot stand alone: 10 and 20 are allowed, while 06 and 30 are not. A string that admits no complete split has result zero.

Different splits count separately even when they have equal-length prefixes. For example, 226 can be divided as 2|2|6, 22|6, or 2|26. Do not decode and return the letters; the required output is just the number of valid splits. Count without listing every possible string of letters, which becomes prohibitively expensive on long inputs of ones.

Example 1:

Input: s = "226"
Output: 3

Example 2:

Input: s = "06"
Output: 0

Example 3:

Input: s = "2101"
Output: 1

Constraints:

  • 1 <= s.length <= 90
  • s contains only digits 0 through 9.
  • The total number of decodings fits a signed 32-bit integer for the supplied inputs.
